column2: On the authority of Abū Masʿūd [ʿUqbah] ibn ʿAmr al-Anṣārī al-Badrī (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Among the words that people have received from the earliest prophethood is: If you feel no shame, then do as you wish.” Reported by al-Bukhārī.
Adraka al-nās (“people have received”): they inherited it generation after generation.

Adraka means “reached”. “From the earliest prophethood”: that which came before our Prophet ﷺ. Idhā lam tastaḥi (“if you feel no shame”): modesty (ḥayāʾ) is a trait that urges doing what is fine and leaving what is ugly, and it has other definitions. “Then do as you wish”: whatever you want.
The nobility of modesty, for there is no prophet who did not urge it, and it was not abrogated.
It is modesty that restrains a person and deters him from sins and from engaging in anything the Sharīʿah deems ugly.
Whoever is not characterised by modesty does whatever he wishes, good or evil.
A point of benefit:
One of the scholars said: This hadith contains the five rulings, in his words, “If you feel no shame, then do as you wish”,

because a person's deed is either something to be ashamed of or not: the first is the unlawful and the disliked, and the second the obligatory, the recommended and the permissible. That is why it has been said that Islam revolves around this hadith.

This hadith makes clear to us that modesty has always been praised, approved and commanded in the revealed laws, and it was not abrogated as other things were, because the sound [mind] approves of it and desires it, for modesty does not enter anything without adorning it, nor is it removed from anything without disfiguring it.
Whoever is deprived of modesty is deprived of much good. If a person has no modesty to drive him to do what is fine and to noble character,
and to keep him far from everything ugly and evil, then let him do whatever his soul, which commands evil, bids him, whatever it may be, for Allah will recompense him for his deed.
The command here is for threat, as in the saying of the Exalted, “Do whatever you wish” [Fuṣṣilat 41:40]. It may carry another meaning:

that if you want to do something, and it is something you need not be ashamed of doing, whether before Allah, lest He punish you for it, or before people, lest they blame you for doing it, then do as you wish, for it is permissible for you; and otherwise do not.
Among what has been said in censure of one who has no shame:
If you do not fear the consequence of the nights, / and feel no shame, then do as you wish.
By Allah, there is no good in life, / nor in this world, once modesty is gone.
And another poet:
If you do not guard your honour, nor fear the Creator, / nor feel shame before any creature, then do whatever you wish.
Another poet:
Many a shameful deed has nothing come between me / and committing it except modesty.
It was the cure for it; but / when modesty is gone, there is no cure.
